description: We are engineering students specializing in software and Ai, driven by a passion for AI, data analysis, and building impactful, real-world tech solutions. For this NASA Space Apps Challenge, we are tackling the "Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions" challenge
summary: AstroCare Copilot is an offline health assistant for astronauts on deep-space missions. It learns each astronaut's personal baseline, detects early drift across six areas (cardiovascular, bone and muscle, immunity and sleep, metabolic and nutrition, mental and social, radiation), explains every alert in plain words, and recommends concrete actions. Because Mars is up to about 20 minutes away by radio, the crew must be medically autonomous: AstroCare runs entirely on board and prepares a compact, prioritised packet for the ground team. It follows NASA's five hazards of human spaceflight, and the same approach can support remote and polar communities on Earth.
details: AstroCare Copilot compares each astronaut's daily signals (heart rate and variability, blood pressure, glucose, temperature, sleep, mood, fatigue, exercise, voice, social time, immune stress, radiation dose rate) with that astronaut's own baseline. Drift scores and an Isolation Forest flag early decline. Every alert explains why in plain words, is colour-coded green, amber or red, and is tagged with its NASA hazard. A Self-check tab takes blood pressure, heart rate, glucose, temperature, sleep and mood and shows what to do now, how to prevent worsening and when to contact the ground. Also included: a daily routine with points, a 30-day what-if twin, crew tension and isolation view, local voice-stress analysis, four environments (transit, station, lunar base, Mars) and an Earth packet queued offline during radio delay. Built with Python, scikit-learn, pandas, SQLite and Streamlit, plus a WebXR VR habitat and an offline mobile app. It runs on board without internet. Limits: decision support, not diagnosis; demo crew data is SIMULATED; reference ranges need clinician review; about 3% false alarms in 30 simulated runs. Demo tip: in the live app, choose Amira and slide to mission day 44 to see the early warning. Live app: https://astrocare-copilot-neus8cerqkh83r6pkm3jak.streamlit.app/ Landing page (VR, mobile): https://khadija12-tech.github.io/astrocare-copilot/ Code: https://github.com/khadija12-tech/astrocare-copilot
